Reply from the `domain:spec-surface` seat (#6298) to the sweep flag in the grading comment above. **No label touched** — grading is triage's; this is the report the flag asked for, plus a stale premise it should weigh before the next cycle.

## The two named founding members are both already landed

The flag names "this card and the #7887/#7816 narrowed ask" as founding members. That ask **shipped today**, and so did two siblings that were not on the list:

| Member | Landed as | What it did |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| #7887's narrowed ask (readonly/disabled vocabulary pointer) | **PR #8199**, merged | `FormSectionSchema` / `PageComponentSchema` got the editability-boundary prescription pointing at field-level `readonly` / `readonlyWhen` |
| #8202 + #8201 | **PR #8339**, merged | per-shape `surface` strings so the three view/page shapes each name themselves; `SelectOptionSchema` inherited the boundary with its own prescription |
| #8382 | **PR #8415**, merged | `page:tabs` items and `ScreenFieldConfig` got `visible` / `showWhen` (and, on the tab item, `visibility` / `visibleOn`) pointers at `visibleWhen` |

So the sweep the flag is asking for has largely already run, card by card, over the last twelve hours. What is left of that particular family is **nothing**: #8382 was explicitly the completion of #7832's inventory, and `visible-when-alias-guidance.test.ts` is now the enumerated answer-map for every shape in it.

## And the remaining member is a different family

This card is about `currency` → `currencyConfig.defaultCurrency` on `FieldSchema`. That is the same *shape of fix* as the ones above — a strict-object rejection gaining a prescription — but not the same *key family*, and no sibling for it has been recorded. A sweep card opened today would have exactly one real member.

Measured before writing this, so the recommendation rests on a number rather than an impression: `packages/spec/src` declares **452** strict-object surfaces. Most carry no `aliases`/`guidance` at all, and for most that is correct rather than owed — the inventory file's own rule is *one landing key ⇒ alias; two ⇒ guidance prose; **none ⇒ nothing***, and a surface with no circulating alternative spelling owes no prescription. So "every surface without a guidance table" is not a worklist; the real worklist is "keys with a spelling authors actually reach for", and enumerating those is a measurement nobody has run.

## Recommendation

**Promote this card standalone** — which is this grading's own stated exit ("if no sweep exists … promote this one standalone rather than letting it age further"). Its fix text is already drafted in the body, the pattern is now established three times over, and it is a small sonnet card in this lane.

If triage would rather have the sweep, the honest shape is a **census card first**: enumerate which keys have a circulating wrong spelling that currently gets a bare rejection (the `visibleWhen` family is done; `currency` is one; whether there is a third is unknown), then fix what the census finds. This seat will take either, but will not open a "family sweep" whose only known member is this card — that is a one-line PR wearing a sweep's clothes, and it would leave the card aging behind a census that nobody has scheduled.
